content:
Last year we announced AlphaProof and its collaboration with AlphaGeometry on the 2024 IMO, and promised in our blog post that we would release more technical details about AlphaProof soon.

We're pleased to share the wait is now over, and that the details about this system from the 2024 IMO can be found in (the preview of) our Nature paper "Olympiad-Level Formal Mathematical Reasoning with Reinforcement Learning" (link for people without Nature access). Included are evaluations on PutnamBench, miniF2F, and our new Lean IMO benchmark formal-imo.

As many of you know, a key goal for us has been to get AlphaProof into the hands of mathematicians. We are also excited to share an update on this front.

We have now developed a VSCode extension for interacting with AlphaProof, and as a first step, we are beginning to share it with a small, private group of trusted testers to gather initial feedback. This is a crucial phase that will allow us to iterate quickly and improve the tool before any wider release.

We are still in the very early stages of this process and access remains highly limited. However, for those who are deeply interested in providing early feedback and helping to shape the tool's future, you can register your interest via the form at https://deepmind.google/alphaproof.

Please understand that we will only be able to onboard new testers very gradually as we scale up. We appreciate your patience, and are incredibly excited about the journey to making AlphaProof a useful collaborator for the mathematics community.
